stories.title: Lateral photovoltaic infrared detectors with colloidal quantum dots
stories.description: Colloidal quantum dots have ushered in solution-processable infrared detectors, promising a low-cost technology for diverse applications. However, their performance, limited by low external quantum efficiency and high noise currents, continues to lag behind state-of-the-art single-crystal devices. Earlier quantum dot photovoltaic detectors used vertical stacks in which the nanoparticle film is sandwiched between conductive electrode layers that limit infrared transmission. Here we show that coating thin films of HgTe quantum dots directly on interdigitated Au/Ti and Pt electrodes, before capping the dots with a protective polymer layer, leverages the asymmetric metal–Hg interactions to create a lateral p–n junction. This approach eliminates the top electrode, creates optical resonances that boost light collection and provides efficient carrier collection by matching the electrode gaps to the carrier diffusion lengths. The resulting detectors, based on mid-wave infrared quantum dots, achieve 70% external quantum efficiency at 4 µm and background-limited performance at 160 K, and retain 95% of their initial performance after seven months. By simply tuning quantum dot size, we further demonstrate spectrally versatile infrared detection across the short- and long-wave regimes. A photovoltaic device that uses HgTe colloidal quantum dot films deposited on interdigitated Au/Ti and Pt electrodes exploits asymmetric metal–Hg interactions to form lateral p–n junctions with efficient carrier collection by matching the electrode gaps to the carrier diffusion lengths, enabling high-performance infrared photodetectors.

stories.title: Quantum-resistant hybrid cryptographic framework with adaptive authentication for secure IoT-enabled healthcare systems
stories.description: The rapid adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in healthcare has introduced significant security and privacy challenges due to the sensitivity of medical data and the resource constraints of connected devices. This paper proposes a quantum-resistant hybrid cryptographic framework that integrates lattice-based key encapsulation with elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) to ensure secure and efficient communication in IoT-enabled healthcare systems. The framework incorporates an adaptive multi-factor authentication mechanism driven by contextual risk assessment and a lightweight distributed ledger for tamper-evident audit trails. A three-tier architecture spanning device, gateway, and cloud layers is designed to balance security and performance. Experimental evaluation using real-world medical datasets demonstrates an intrusion detection rate of 97.8%, a 34% reduction in computational overhead compared to conventional approaches, and end-to-end latency below 150 ms. The results confirm that the proposed framework provides a scalable and future-ready solution for securing healthcare IoT systems against both classical and quantum threats.

stories.title: Domain-generalized dual-branch attention fusion network for cross-dataset Chinese traditional instrument family classification
stories.description: Automatic recognition of Chinese traditional instruments is important for music information retrieval and digital music archives, but models trained on a single dataset often suffer from cross-dataset distribution shifts. To address this problem, we propose DG-DBAFNet, a domain-generalized dual-branch attention fusion network for family-level Chinese traditional instrument classification. Each audio clip is represented as a three-channel MFCC-CQT-Chroma time-frequency representation. The model extracts complementary features through an acoustic attention branch and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 branch, and dynamically integrates them using an adaptive gated fusion module. To improve single-source generalization, MixStyle, domain-robust supervised contrastive learning, and pseudo-domain adversarial learning are incorporated during training. Trained only on CTIS and evaluated on CTIS and two unseen external datasets, ChMusic and FolkMusic, DG-DBAFNet achieved Macro F1 scores of 97.42%, 62.42%, and 51.38%, respectively, outperforming traditional machine-learning, CNN-based, attention-based, pretrained, and transformer baselines. These results suggest that complementary branch fusion and pseudo-domain robust optimization can improve the robustness of Chinese traditional instrument recognition under cross-dataset distribution shifts.

stories.title: A complete telomere-to-telomere genome assembly for silver perch (Bidyanus bidyanus)
stories.description: Silver perch (Bidyanus bidyanus) is a freshwater teleost species indigenous to southeastern Australia. Owing to its fast growth and strong environmental adaptability, it holds considerable potential for commercial aquaculture. Currently, there isn’t yet a high-quality genome for this species. Our study presents the first gapless T2T genome for silver perch, which was constructed using PacBio HiFi, ONT, and Hi-C data, as well as short reads. The resulting assembly spanned 679.72 Mb and achieved a scaffold N50 of 29.95 Mb, with sequences anchored onto 24 chromosomes and telomeric repeats identified at both chromosomal termini. Genome annotation identified 25,240 putative protein-coding genes. BUSCO and Compleasm analyses yielded completeness scores of 99.75% and 99.97%, respectively. This result will advance both population genetics and conservation efforts for silver perch, while also serving as a key resource for optimizing its selective breeding.

stories.title: Age-dependent progenitor switching shapes adult brown adipose tissue heterogeneity
stories.description: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) burns chemical energy to generate heat and supports whole-body metabolism. BAT is continuously renewed from adipose progenitor cells (APCs), yet which progenitors sustain the tissue during adulthood, and how this changes with age, remain unclear. Here we show that Pdgfra+ APCs, which build BAT early in life, contribute little to its renewal in adult mice. Using single-cell analysis and lineage tracing, we identify a previously unrecognized population of Myl1-expressing APCs that emerges with age and becomes the major source of new brown fat cells in adult and middle-aged mice. These Myl1+ APC-derived adipocytes adopt a distinct metabolic state, favouring oxidative phosphorylation over glycolysis, which contributes to the metabolic heterogeneity of adult BAT. Ablating Myl1+ APC-derived adipocytes, or blocking their differentiation, reduces BAT mass and impairs glucose control. Our findings reveal an age-dependent ‘progenitor switch’ that drives the renewal and functional heterogeneity of adult brown fat. While Pdgfra+ progenitors shape brown adipose tissue in early life, a distinct population of Myl1+ progenitors predominantly differentiates into brown adipocytes in BAT of adult and middle-aged mice and modulates systemic glucose metabolism in mice.

stories.title: An amorphous electrocatalyst enables efficient and stable hydrogen production from seawater at 1 A cm−2 for over 9,000 h
stories.description: Hydrogen production through seawater electrolysis is typically hindered by corrosion caused by Cl−. Protective layers on catalysts can resist corrosion, yet the addition of such layers can inhibit access to active sites. Therefore, maintaining exposed active sites to achieve operational stability and good performance remains a challenging balance. Here we report an amorphous material, namely, Ni@Mo-CoOx, that serves as both a protective layer and an effective catalyst for seawater splitting. The amorphous layer resists Cl− corrosion, stabilizes embedded particles to promote hydrogen evolution and accelerates water dissociation. Ni@Mo-CoOx can drive hydrogen production from natural seawater at 1,000 mA cm−2 with an overpotential of 187 mV, and maintain performance for 9,000 h. A noble-metal-free anion exchange membrane seawater electrolyser with a Ni@Mo-CoOx cathode is assembled and operates stably at 1.0 A cm−2 for 1,000 h with a cell voltage of 1.81 V at 60 °C. Corrosion is a prominent pathway for catalyst deactivation in seawater electrolysis. Here an amorphous electrocatalyst is developed to act as a protection layer that is also effective for hydrogen evolution from seawater. Current densities reach 1 A cm−2 at an overpotential of 187 mV with stable operation for over 9,000 h.

stories.description: Citizen has unveiled two Exceed Brilliant Pearl limited editions that pair mother-of-pearl inner bezels with a solar-powered Eco-Drive movement, radio-controlled timekeeping, and an automatically adjusting moonphase display. Limited to 350 pieces each, the duo will go on sale in Japan in December.

stories.title: Intel handheld vs AMD Ryzen Mini PC: MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ can double as work PC
stories.description: YouTuber ETA Prime has put the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ handheld console against the Morefine AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 Mini PC to see if the MSI handheld can double as a capable work PC. The testing proves that the Claw 8 EX AI+ can indeed function as a standalone productivity computer thanks to the Intel Arc G3 Extreme SoC.
